infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: node/kube-infer-58 moved to NotReady in cluster infer-usw at 2026-03-14T21:10:56Z (auto-detected heartbeat loss)

alex (oncall): saw it. paging now. are we seeing impact to inference pools?

devin: yep, `infer-usw-pool-a` lost 3 pods that were pinned to that node, autoscaler moved some work but tail latency spiked ~300ms for a subset of requests. metrics: 95th went from 220ms -> 540ms across the pool.

lina: checking node kubelet logs now. attaching snippet: ```Mar 14 21:09:32 kube-infer-58 kubelet[1234]: E0321 21:09:32 kubelet_kubelet.go:123] Runtime failed: containerd: failed to start container: error initializing device plugin: nvidia: driver crash: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
Mar 14 21:09:33 kube-infer-58 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=6/ABRT```

alex (oncall): CUDA driver crash -> kubelet restart -> Node NotReady makes sense. any OOMs? were pods OOMKilled?

devin: two inference containers show `OOMKilled` in pod events just before the driver crash. GPU memory pressure looks high based on prometheus `nvidia_gpu_memory_used` for that node—near 98% for a couple of long-lived sessions.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-07 (kube-infer-58 node flap) — severity P2. Paging: @sre-rotations, @alex (oncall).

alex (oncall): I'm going to cordon the node to prevent new pods: `kubectl cordon kube-infer-58` — doing it now.

alex (oncall): `kubectl drain kube-infer-58 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` queued, but a few pods are stuck terminating because GV NIC teardown errors.

lina: I can ssh and forcibly kill the stuck containers to speed drain. before I do that, suggestion: move hot traffic off the pool by toggling route weight to `infer-usw-fallback` 100% for 5m. that will reduce pressure while we recover.

devin: agreed. initiating traffic cutover via routing API: `POST /routing/weight` payload -> set `infer-usw-pool-a` 0, `infer-usw-fallback` 100. ETA ~30s.

infra-bot: Routing change applied: all traffic moved to infer-usw-fallback.

alex (oncall): good. that should reduce customer-visible latency. recording customer impact: ~12% of requests hit higher p95 during spike window, ~4 customers saw request timeouts (retries succeeded). tagging accounts: acme-corp, quickchat, helpdesk-inc.

lina: I'm on the node. saw kernel taints related to NVidia drivers after driver restart. running `dmesg | tail -n 40` shows repeated `nvidia: GPU has fallen off the bus` messages. suspect hardware flakiness or driver bug under high memory churn.

devin: for short term, let's recreate the kubelet process to re-establish device plugin cleanly. lina, if you can `systemctl restart kubelet` after killing lingering containers, that may get the node back to Ready. but keep it cordoned to prevent scheduling until we confirm stability.

lina: doing `pkill -f infer-runtime && systemctl restart kubelet` now. I'll watch node status.

(approx 90s pause)

lina: kubelet came back up but node cycles NotReady -> Ready -> NotReady twice. kernel still logs occasional `GPU reset failed`.

alex (oncall): rolling out a safer recovery: mark node unschedulable permanently for the incident, then spin up a replacement from pool `infer-usw-spare` to restore capacity and then migrate workloads. I'll request 2x replacement machines.

devin: requested 2 replacements via infra autoscale group with tag `infer-usw-spare` — provisioning now. predicted ready in ~3m.

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: 2 instances requested for group infer-usw-spare.

lina: for immediate relief I will evict remaining inference pods from the problematic node forcibly: `kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0 --force` for the 3 stuck pods.

alex (oncall): go ahead. note to SRE: set an alert rule to catch `nvidia_gpu_memory_used > 95%` sustained for >60s; we didn't have that threshold tight enough and it would've given earlier warning.

sre-rotations: noted, will open PR to adjust prometheus alert.

devin: replacement nodes are booting, kubelets in them are stable; new pods are scheduling to `infer-usw-spare`. tail latency going back to baseline on fallback pool, and overall 95th trending down.

lina: re: root cause prelim: sequence looks like sustained GPU mem pressure -> some containers OOMGPU (OOMKilled) -> nvidia driver experiences a fatal condition -> kernel resets GPU -> kubelet aborts on device plugin error and restarts -> node NotReady. hardware flake not ruled out; need deeper driver logs and possibly repro with long-running pinned sessions.

alex (oncall): runbook actions completed: node cordoned, pod eviction forced, traffic cutover to fallback, replacements requested. Next steps: detailed post-incident trace, collect `dmesg`, `journalctl -u kubelet`, container logs, nvidia-smi output and upload to S3 bucket `inc-logs/INC-2026-0314-07/` for RCA. assign to devin for RCA writeup.

devin: will collect artifacts and start RCA. I'll include memory profiles and correlate customer sessions. targeting preliminary RCA within 24h.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-0314-07 updated: status -> mitigating.

alex (oncall): handing off at 22:00 UTC to night oncall @lina. please monitor the replaced nodes and re-enable routing incrementally when stable. leaving cordon on kube-infer-58 for now.

lina: ack. I'll monitor and escalate to infra if we see more `GPU has fallen off the bus` across multiple hosts. updating incident notes. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by lina.

alex (oncall): closing active pager for me. if anything else pops, wake me.

(END THREAD)
